howto.name: Upload an image
howto.text: Drop a JPG, PNG, WEBP, HEIC, BMP, GIF, or TIFF — up to 50 MB.

howto.name: Pick a rotation angle
howto.text: Click 90° (left/right), 180°, 270°, or enter any custom angle (e.g. 13° to straighten a tilted scan). The canvas auto-expands so nothing is cropped off.

howto.name: Click Rotate
howto.text: Output downloads as the same format you uploaded; transparency is preserved for PNG and WEBP.

faq.a: For 90°/180°/270° rotations no — they're lossless transpositions of pixels. Arbitrary angles re-sample using bicubic interpolation which is visually near-lossless but technically introduces sub-pixel smoothing.

faq.q: Why is my output bigger than the input?
faq.a: For non-90° angles, the rotated rectangle no longer fits in the original bounding box. The canvas auto-expands so the whole rotated image is visible (corners get transparent/white padding).
Yes — the alpha channel is preserved, and rotated corners are transparent (not white) for PNG and WEBP. For JPG the corners get white since JPG has no alpha.
